notes: EPT (mayfly/stonefly/caddisfly) taxa richness; more sensitive taxa indicate better condition.
Benthic Shannon diversity; higher diversity indicates better condition.
Percent tolerant individuals; a higher share of pollution-tolerant taxa indicates worse condition.
Chlorophyll a; higher indicates algal enrichment/eutrophication (worse).
Total nitrogen; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse). The total fraction, reported in every NRSA cycle, and the fraction published nitrogen criteria are written against.
pH degrades condition at BOTH extremes. Two-sided (optimum) curve: scored 1.0 across the reference interquartile core, falling in both tails.
Total phosphorus; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse).
Turbidity; higher indicates more suspended sediment (worse).

Percent of native fish individuals that are simple lithophils, spawning on clean coarse substrate without nest building; higher is better. Reproduction depends on substrate that fine sediment smothers.

Native non-tolerant fish taxa richness (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is better. Total richness need not fall under disturbance, because tolerant species replace intolerant ones; this counts only the taxa that do not tolerate it.
Percent of native fish taxa not classed tolerant (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is better. A proportion, so it does not carry the size of a region's species pool the way a richness count does.
Percent of native fish individuals classed tolerant (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is worse. Dominance by tolerant fish is a standard multimetric-index component of disturbance.
Native fish taxa richness; higher is better.

Log relative bed stability; departure from the reference core in EITHER direction departs from reference (negative excess fines, positive an armored, sediment-starved bed, the classic below-impoundment failure). The pilot's rising direction scored armored beds 1.0 and left Sediment continuity blind to its textbook failure mode. Two-sided form is an owner decision at the adversarial review gate, 2026-08-21.
Log mean substrate diameter; coarser substrate generally better, but valley-type dependent.
Percent fast-water (riffle/run) habitat; more generally better for many biota. Ecoregion-dependent.
Percent sand and fines; higher indicates fine-sediment loading (worse).
Residual pool depth per 100 m; deeper residual pools generally better habitat.
Channel sinuosity; higher generally indicates a more natural planform.

Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
Mean bankfull height; both incision (very high banks) and over-widening (very low) depart from reference. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.
Mid-channel canopy density; higher shading generally better for thermal/light regime.
Riparian canopy plus mid-layer plus ground cover; higher is better.
Percent embeddedness; higher means interstitial spaces filled with fines (worse).
Natural fish cover; higher is better.

Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.

Watershed wetland (%), woody plus herbaceous, both classes required; wetlands store surface water and attenuate flow peaks. EASI scores Surface water storage on the same sum (method watershed-wetland-extent).
Mean watershed elevation; physiographic scaling context. Predictor only.
Mean annual precipitation (1981-2010 normal); scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.
Mean annual runoff; scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.

chem_NTL.notes: Total nitrogen; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse). The total fraction, reported in every NRSA cycle, and the fraction published nitrogen criteria are written against.

chem_PH.caveat: pH carries natural geology (calcareous or naturally acidic waters) as well as disturbance, and a two-sided core narrower than measurement precision is noise rather than condition.
chem_PH.notes: pH degrades condition at BOTH extremes. Two-sided (optimum) curve: scored 1.0 across the reference interquartile core, falling in both tails.

chem_PTL.notes: Total phosphorus; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse).

chem_TURB.notes: Turbidity; higher indicates more suspended sediment (worse).

fish_NAT_LITHPIND.notes: Percent of native fish individuals that are simple lithophils, spawning on clean coarse substrate without nest building; higher is better. Reproduction depends on substrate that fine sediment smothers.

fish_NAT_NTOLNTAX.notes: Native non-tolerant fish taxa richness (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is better. Total richness need not fall under disturbance, because tolerant species replace intolerant ones; this counts only the taxa that do not tolerate it.

fish_NAT_NTOLPTAX.notes: Percent of native fish taxa not classed tolerant (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is better. A proportion, so it does not carry the size of a region's species pool the way a richness count does.

fish_NAT_TOLRPIND.notes: Percent of native fish individuals classed tolerant (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is worse. Dominance by tolerant fish is a standard multimetric-index component of disturbance.

fish_NAT_TOTLNTAX.notes: Native fish taxa richness; higher is better.

phab_LRBS_use.notes: Log relative bed stability; departure from the reference core in EITHER direction departs from reference (negative excess fines, positive an armored, sediment-starved bed, the classic below-impoundment failure). The pilot's rising direction scored armored beds 1.0 and left Sediment continuity blind to its textbook failure mode. Two-sided form is an owner decision at the adversarial review gate, 2026-08-21.

phab_LSUB_DMM.notes: Log mean substrate diameter; coarser substrate generally better, but valley-type dependent.

phab_PCT_FAST.notes: Percent fast-water (riffle/run) habitat; more generally better for many biota. Ecoregion-dependent.

phab_PCT_SAFN.notes: Percent sand and fines; higher indicates fine-sediment loading (worse).

phab_RP100_cm.notes: Residual pool depth per 100 m; deeper residual pools generally better habitat.

phab_SINU.notes: Channel sinuosity; higher generally indicates a more natural planform.

phab_XBKA.notes: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.

phab_XBKF_H.notes: Mean bankfull height; both incision (very high banks) and over-widening (very low) depart from reference. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.

phab_XCDENMID.notes: Mid-channel canopy density; higher shading generally better for thermal/light regime.

phab_XCMGW.notes: Riparian canopy plus mid-layer plus ground cover; higher is better.

phab_XEMBED.notes: Percent embeddedness; higher means interstitial spaces filled with fines (worse).

phab_XFC_NAT.notes: Natural fish cover; higher is better.

bfiws.caveat: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.
bfiws.notes: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.

pctwet2019ws.caveat: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.
pctwet2019ws.notes: Watershed wetland (%), woody plus herbaceous, both classes required; wetlands store surface water and attenuate flow peaks. EASI scores Surface water storage on the same sum (method watershed-wetland-extent).

DrainageAreaClass.notes: Watershed drainage area class. Breakpoints 10 and 100 km2 are fixed constants.
DrainageAreaClass.rationale: Drainage area is the primary scaling variable for channel geometry, discharge and assemblage composition. 10 km2 separates headwaters from wadeable small streams; 100 km2 separates small streams from larger wadeable rivers. Both are conventional round-number breaks in NRSA and NHDPlus practice, not sample quantiles.

ChannelSlopeClass.notes: Reach channel slope class. Breakpoints 0.5 and 2 percent are fixed constants.
ChannelSlopeClass.rationale: Channel slope controls stream power, substrate sorting and channel type. 0.5 and 2 percent are the conventional low gradient, moderate and steep breaks used in Rosgen-family and Montgomery-Buffington channel typing. National median slope is near 0.13 percent, so this ladder is eligible in roughly half of L3 ecoregions; it is screened where it qualifies and excluded with a recorded reason where it does not.

NhdSlopeClass.notes: NHDPlus V2 flowline slope. Adopted by the national scale analysis (rule STRAT-10).

elevws.notes: Mean watershed elevation; physiographic scaling context. Predictor only.

precip8110ws.notes: Mean annual precipitation (1981-2010 normal); scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.

runoffws.notes: Mean annual runoff; scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 24 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 1 curve is fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 2 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 1 carries the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.204 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.24 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. The NARS-9 pool (XER): In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The Level II pool (10.1): In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The Level I pool (10): In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 77 matched national donors, but in the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. 223 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but in the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include no regional criterion for conductivity. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

referenceSupport.transferNote: 66 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region XER, 18 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, air temperature. Every station drains to this ecoregion's faunal province. The national scale analysis supports this metric at Level II, finer than the level borrowed from, so the transfer risk is moderate and the expectation may not represent local conditions.

phab_PCT_FAST.methodContext: At each thalweg station record the channel unit (falls, cascade, rapid, riffle, glide, pool, dry). The value is the percent of stations in fast water (falls, cascade, rapid or riffle).

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

phab_PCT_SAFN.methodContext: Record the size class of the particle at five evenly spaced points across each of the 11 transects and the 10 cross-sections midway between them (105 particles). The value is the percent of particles that are sand or finer.

referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to least-disturbed stations selected by a fixed landscape-pressure screen.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

phab_RP100_cm.methodContext: Measure the thalweg depth at 10 or 15 evenly spaced stations between each pair of transects (100 or 150 along the reach). The value is the mean residual pool depth in centimeters, computed from that depth profile and the reach slope with the NRSA physical habitat calculations.

referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to least-disturbed stations selected by a fixed landscape-pressure screen.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

phab_SINU.methodContext: Take a compass bearing (backsight) and the distance between each pair of neighboring transects. The value is the channel length along those segments divided by the straight line distance between the ends of the reach.

referenceSupport.screen: least-disturbed-regional-v1 (relaxed tier, watershed agriculture at most 25 percent, the 25 percent floor)
referenceSupport.transferNote: 22 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) of this ecoregion.
referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to least-disturbed stations selected by a fixed landscape-pressure screen.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

phab_XBKA.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to least-disturbed stations selected by a fixed landscape-pressure screen.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

phab_XBKF_H.methodContext: At each transect, measure the height of the bankfull elevation above the present water surface in meters, with a rod at the water's edge and a clinometer held level at bankfull. The value is the mean of the 11 heights.

referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to least-disturbed stations selected by a fixed landscape-pressure screen.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

phab_XCDENMID.methodContext: At mid-channel on each transect, read a convex spherical densiometer facing upstream, downstream, left and right, counting the covered points of 17. The value is the mean of the 44 readings as a percent.

referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to least-disturbed stations selected by a fixed landscape-pressure screen.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

phab_XCMGW.methodContext: In a 10 m by 10 m plot on each bank at each transect, estimate the areal cover class of woody vegetation in the canopy, the understory and the ground layer. The value is the summed woody cover of the three layers, averaged over the 22 plots, as a fraction.

referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to least-disturbed stations selected by a fixed landscape-pressure screen.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

phab_XEMBED.methodContext: At five evenly spaced points across each of the 11 transects, estimate how much of the particle under the point is buried in sand and finer sediment, in percent. Record the 55 estimates. The value is their mean.

referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to least-disturbed stations selected by a fixed landscape-pressure screen.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

phab_XFC_NAT.methodContext: In the 10 m of channel centered on each transect, estimate the areal cover class of each fish cover type on the form (wood, brush, overhanging vegetation, undercut banks, boulders and the rest). The value is the summed areal cover of the types that are not man-made, averaged over the transects.

referenceSupport.transferNote: 204 least-disturbed stations from the national pool whose natural setting falls inside this ecoregion's comparability envelope, none inside this ecoregion. Every donor drains to this ecoregion's faunal province.
referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own.
referenceSupport.basisLimit: The donor stations lie outside this ecoregion and its parents, matched on natural setting rather than drawn from it.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

The reference pool's lower quartile for this metric is zero: at least a quarter of the pool has a value of zero, so the curve has no fitted lower anchor. It rises in a straight line from 0 at zero to 1 at 3, the pool's upper quartile. Read the band as a coarse sort, not a measurement.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from NARS-9 region ecoregion XER because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 66 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region XER, 18 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, air temperature. Every station drains to this ecoregion's faunal province. The national scale analysis supports this metric at Level II, finer than the level borrowed from, so the transfer risk is moderate and the expectation may not represent local conditions.
